copy.headline: OIL RETURNS. THE BOTTLENECK DOES NOT.
copy.deck: The IEA measures rising October crude supply and floating stocks, yet on-land inventories shrink and diesel stays scarce. A Reuters survey of China's AI infrastructure reveals the same analytical trap: planned projects are not delivered processors.
copy.mechanism: Aggregate supply and investment totals obscure where usable inventories and actual components are located.
copy.chainNote: GULF CRUDE EXPORTS → OIL ON WATER → GLOBAL INVENTORIES; DIESEL STILL TIGHT
copy.evidenceNote: The IEA's November 13 report measures October changes and forecasts fourth-quarter balances. No 13 November increase in safe physical throughput is established.
copy.footer: CRUDE ≠ DIESEL · FLOATING ≠ AVAILABLE · PROJECT ≠ HARDWARE
